name: Poaching Ivory
beta: Start by stepping off a neighbouring boulder, then clip a trio of bolts up the face on the far-right line.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: rightmost of the three bolted lines, starting from a nearby boulder

name: No Biggy
beta: Go straight up beyond the first bolt of Cling Peaches. A second bolt and some marginal nuts are all the protection on this long single pitch.
overview: One long, serious pitch that heads directly upward from the first bolt of the neighbouring route. A single further bolt plus marginal nut placements make up the protection.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Straight up from the first bolt of Cling Peaches

name: Pony Express
beta: Two bolts guard the lower face; swing left of the shrubbery and carry on higher to a shelf, where the rap anchor sits on the right.
overview: A bolted face leads past the left side of some bushes, then an upper face reaches a ledge that holds the rappel anchor.

current.area_walk_in: The way in passes through a notch in the rock before reaching the wall.
current.descent: rappel from the ledge
current.anchor: rappel anchor sitting at the ledge's right end

name: Pop Rocks
beta: Ascend the face directly, clipping a lone bolt, to reach a good crack; shift left, then climb vertically and pull the overhang to finish.
overview: A face-to-crack route high in the valley that finishes by surmounting an overhang.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: near the top end of Rock Garden Valley

name: Primal Flake
beta: Climb the opening face with two bolts for protection, then shuffle hand-over-hand along that flake until a bolt. Work rightward and upward into an overhanging corner and carry on to the top.
overview: A route on the dome's southeastern shoulder that links a short face section to a hand traverse along a feature called the Primal Flake, finishing via an overhang or corner to the summit.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: along the dome's southeast shoulder

name: Punish the Mosquito
beta: Three bolts protect the climbing, beginning from the black stretch of wall.
overview: A bolted line that starts in a dark patch of rock well right of its neighbours.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: approx. 150 ft beyond Sendero Luminoso, from a dark band of rock

name: Pure and Easy
beta: Begin in the big corner facing left, clip the bolt, then angle up leftward across plates and reach a belay ledge.
overview: Climbs the big corner to a bolt, then slants up-left over plates, arriving at a ledge for belaying.

current.descent: tunnel right, then rap 80 ft down a ramp
current.location: big corner facing left

name: Quadrophenia
beta: Start in a flake facing right beside a tree, climb it, then work up the grainy wall past a bolt that has no hanger, reaching a top with a rap anchor.
overview: Climbs a flake and then grainy face, clipping a bolt that lacks its hanger, to a summit. Casual 5.7 leaders should look elsewhere.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: flake facing right, beside a tree on its left, 75 ft along from Pure and Easy

name: Quaking Has-Beens
beta: Three bolts lead you straight up the southeast face of the pinnacle.
overview: A bolted face on the southeast side of the right-most pinnacle, with an unfinished line beside it.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: rightmost pinnacle

name: Quivering Savages
beta: Trace a row of bolts into a corner that faces left, then work leftward and up to finish.
overview: The bolts lead into a corner facing left, after which the line works up and leftward to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Racing Stripes
beta: Climb the crack and chimney leaving the alcove, clipping bolts and adding nuts and cams; after leaving the chimney, move right past a last bolt to the anchors. It can be climbed first to rig a top rope on the neighbouring route.
overview: A pleasantly varied route that mixes crack, chimney and face climbing, rising from the alcove left of its neighbour. Bolts supplement natural gear, making it unusual for the area.

current.area_walk_in: Roughly a quarter hour on marked trails from the Bear Gulch day-use area.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.anchor: anchors at the top of Melvin

name: Rainy Day, Dream Away
beta: Begin atop a block and follow a thin crack until a bolt, then continue up a ramp system that leans rightward.
overview: A thin crack leads to a bolt, then a ramp system leaning right continues upward.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: From a block six ft beyond Tumbling Rainbow

name: Raise Your Right Hand
beta: The leftmost of the formation's two lines, protected by a pair of bolts, it works its way up past several horizontal cracks.
overview: The leftmost of two bolted lines, with only two bolts, wandering across some horizontal cracks.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: the leftward line of the pair on this formation

name: Rampage
beta: Beginning alongside the tree, climb the leaning wall; seven bolts run up to the lower-off shuts, so the climbing is fully clipped.
overview: A steeply overhanging bolted line on The Bear. It is pumpy but well supplied with large holds and enormous footholds, and the leaning wall becomes obvious when you are lowered.

current.area_walk_in: Head up the fire road past the cliff, then take the narrow trail that doubles back through manzanita; allow 20 to 45 minutes from the road.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: just right of the tree

name: Rattle and Hum
beta: Start from the notch located above the ledges you traverse in on, trend left, and follow a subtle groove with bolts.
overview: Step left, then follow a subtle groove where bolts protect you.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Red Wall Face
beta: Just three bolts protect it. The crux comes immediately after clip one, after which the angle backs off. A blocky slab sits shortly below the top: the left side gives the gentler exit, whereas the right side offers a brief, mildly runout alternative.
overview: Bolted face that eases after a hard move low down. Near the top a blocky slab offers an easier exit left or a short, slightly runout exit right.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the foot trail westward as it drops, bends right, crosses a former fence line and then runs down a steep ridge toward the sea. At the big outcrop beside the water, go up its east side to the very top rather than descending the sketchy gully on its left. From there a trail winds down, slightly left and then back right, to the Red Slab climbs.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Regular Route
beta: A low bolt covers the opening moves; farther up, trend right past a further bolt and onto the summit.
overview: A brief route up the detached Thumb, beginning where you land after rappelling off the neighbouring Hand. Bolts guard the start and the top.

current.descent: single-rope rappel into the notch
current.location: Beside where parties land after rappelling The Hand

name: Rehab
beta: Launch from a block located twenty feet from Luminous Breast, clip a bolt, then trend up and leftward to merge with Ripples.
overview: Clips past one bolt and then curves up-left to join the line of Ripples.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Off a boulder-like block twenty feet beyond Luminous Breast

name: Repeat After Me
beta: Stay along the formation's right-hand margin and clip all three bolts.
overview: The right-hand line on Perjury Rock, following the formation's right edge with three bolts for protection.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: along the formation's far-right margin

name: Return To Hell
beta: A three-bolt line up a slab streaked with black rock that gets steeper toward the top.
overview: A slab streaked with dark stains that tips steeper near the top, protected by three bolts. An unfinished bolted project sits around the corner on its left.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the canyon wash up to just short of where it swings right and flattens, then head up and right to the high point. The formation is a cluster of separate blocks rather than one single crag.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: the leftmost route on the crag's north face

name: Revenge Of The Herds
beta: Begin in a little chimney, climbing four bolts in all. Past the second, step rightward to find stopper placements, then angle up-left toward bolt three.
overview: Four bolts; after the second, step rightward to a spot that takes stoppers, then back up and over left to bolt three.

current.area_walk_in: Keep heading up the stony slope, bearing right around Tooth Boulder. Over the crest, descend into a concealed valley holding this sizeable formation, where two bolted lines face northeast. It is out of sight within Stirrup Tank's vicinity.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: leftmost of the two bolted lines on the northeast side, beginning in a stubby chimney

name: Rhoid Warrior
beta: Reach the first bolt by moving in sideways, coming from the left side.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: left side of a smooth face, reached by traversing in from the left

name: Robocop meets The Munchkins
beta: Begin on the face's left side, mantel up and rightward onto a horizontal ledge, then climb a shallow depression past three bolts.
overview: Scramble up and rightward onto a ledge-like horizontal, and clip three bolts within a shallow scoop.

current.area_walk_in: Follow the straight approach to Voodoo Dome, descend, and thread the notch separating Wizard Rock from the unnamed cluster to its south. The crag is on a slope to the right and looks southeast. Coming from the dome called No Place Like, go west and then angle uphill over open rocky terrain.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: left end of the southwest-facing face

name: Where Ees De Santa Claus?
beta: Flaky cracks lead upward; clip the bolt close to the finish, then move leftward and top out.
overview: Flaky cracks lead to a bolt close to the top, after which you go left and then upward.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Rear side of the Rock Hudson formation, atop a detached block near the west end

name: Rock Vixen
beta: Starting well to the right of Terrorist, clip a bolt and move into the right-facing corners above.
overview: A short route of corners facing right, taking about a pitch and a half, with a bolt along the way.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: about 30 ft right of where Terrorist begins, below right-facing corners

name: Roy's Route
beta: It can be run as a single very long pitch, or broken at a bolted belay roughly forty feet up.
overview: A well-regarded bolt line that sits one route over from the Butterfly climb, on its right.

current.area_walk_in: From a spot about 150 yards beyond the fork in the wash, head toward the foot of The Dune, then follow the brushy ledge leftward to reach the Buttress routes.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Run from Your Wife
beta: Gain the ledge used by Two Stage, then step rightward to this line and follow its bolts and pin.
overview: A two-bolt line with one fixed pin, reached by moving right from the ledge shared with Two Stage.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: leaves the Two Stage ledge heading right

name: Runaway
beta: Start near the ledge's left end, pull a minuscule roof, clip a bolt, and keep going to the one-bolt belay near the summit.
overview: A short route on Lost Wall that begins from a ledge running along the wall's right side and ends at a belay just under the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Rust Never Sleeps
beta: Glide up and leftward alongside a slanting crack. A cam around half-size fits the crack; otherwise skip it and keep going without protection until the first bolt.
overview: A bolted slab and crack line. Clip 2 bolts on the way up.

current.descent: walk off the south edge

name: Rye Not
beta: Clip the single bolt and finish up a crack that has bushes growing in it.
overview: A route around to the right of So Another with a single bolt, finishing in a bushy crack.

current.location: around the corner and right of So Another

name: Safety Pin
beta: Begin below and rightward of Casual Affair, mantel across a roof, then climb past a pin and a bolt.
overview: Begin by bouldering past a roof, then keep going up using the bolt and piton.

current.location: below and right of Casual Affair

name: Sampson
beta: Follow the big dihedral that faces left and marks the wall's far edge. It is a strenuous line that takes gear poorly, and the finish is an awkward mantel.
overview: A left-facing corner that bounds the wall on the right. Physical, awkward to protect, and finished with an ungainly mantle.

current.location: right edge of the wall, a left-facing corner

name: Save the Last Stance for Me
beta: Scramble from the left onto the ledge at the base, passing a big tree, and climb the plated face on bolts.
overview: The left-hand of two routes on a wall covered in plates, lower down and to the right of its neighbours. It has four bolts with some gaps between them.

current.area_walk_in: A path heading westward dwindles away at the foot of this big rock mass, whose northeast side can be spotted from far off. Routes here begin from a ledge high above the ground; easy scrambling up cracks below gets you onto it.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: left of two lines on a wall covered in plates; reach the base ledge from the left past a big tree

name: Goldfingers
beta: Climb a crack through ribbed, grippy rock to technical yet well-protected moves; seven bolts lead to the chains.
overview: A crack in ribbed rock covered with interesting, high-friction features; the moves are delicate and well protected.

current.area_walk_in: A path climbs a couple of switchbacks over roughly 0.3 mile to a bend opening onto a big view of the quarry; this wall then sits on your left, with the neighbouring wall across from it.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Scandal
beta: Start in a shallow corner with fixed pins, place a medium cam into a pocket, and angle upward and leftward to a comfortable stance at the southeast arete. Clip a bolt, step across onto the principal face, and trend up and rightward past two bolts to a fixed pin lodged in a slim crack. Finally go left to an obvious pocket taking a big cam.
overview: A climb with good moves on sometimes doubtful rock that mixes a shallow corner, a bolted face and a final slab. Above the technical climbing, fourth-class ground leads on to the summit.

current.descent: two-rope rappel down the line
current.location: East face, to the left of the chimney route and beside a wide crack that leans right

name: Leonard-Horsfall
beta: Once above the chimney, take the ramp up and rightward past the pin. Protection calls for medium and large cams.
overview: A route on the south face of Scout Peak that begins in a chimney full of guano that holds a bolt, then follows a ramp rising to the right with a fixed pin along the way.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: On the wide ledge system on the south side, at the chimney full of guano that holds a bolt

name: Tracker
beta: Climb leftward on sound rock past the one bolt, then from the shoulder move left into a second chute, then ascend it as far as the upper shoulder. Finish by scrambling up and leftward.
overview: A route up the northeast face of Scout Peak by way of two chutes, with a single bolt and unprotected ground higher up before it finishes in a scramble.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Reached from above by circling to the northeast side, in a small steep gully

name: Scream Chuck
beta: Begin the way Lascivious Conduct does, then hand-traverse rightward and follow broken cracks up to the anchor bolts.
overview: Begins like Lascivious Conduct, then traverses rightward by hand and follows broken cracks to the anchor bolts.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: shares the start of Lascivious Conduct

name: Seebolt
beta: Share the first ten feet with Crack Kills; step off rightward there and go up clipping four bolts.
overview: A bolted face that borrows the opening moves of Crack Kills before veering off onto four bolts.

current.area_walk_in: A short, level walk of about five minutes from the parking area to the large brown formation, then around its end to the north side. No boulder hopping.

current.location: shares the opening moves of Crack Kills

name: Separation Anxiety
beta: Four bolts lead to the anchor Kola also uses; the first bolt sits close to twenty feet off the ground, so the opening moves are committing.
overview: A four-bolt line with a high first bolt, roughly 20 ft off the ground.

current.area_walk_in: The path starts at the left side of the Bubble beside a lone tree and some shrubs, heads west above an outcrop of loose rock, then crosses a saddle on a slim footpath with small ups and downs. Take the left fork, which drops a little and then climbs again to the foot of the formation, where a tall bolted line stands straight ahead.
